artworks.title: The Wedding of Jason and Creusa
artworks.artist: Master of the Die (after Baldassare Peruzzi)
artworks.description: A Metropolitan Museum print stages the Corinthian wedding Creon arranged for Jason and his daughter Creusa/Glauce — while Medea leads the children away at left. The king of Corinth is the host whose match will burn his house.

artworks.title: Medea, or the Marriage of Jason and Creusa
artworks.description: Rembrandt's etching for Jan Six's Medea freezes Creon's court wedding: Jason and Creusa before the altar. The Corinthian king is the political force who replaces Medea with his daughter — not the Theban uncle of Antigone.

artworks.title: Medea Sarcophagus (Berlin)
artworks.description: Roman sarcophagus in Berlin: Medea's poisoned gifts reach Creusa — the death that Euripides and Apollodorus extend to Creon himself when he clasps his burning daughter. Corinth's king as collateral of the Argonaut divorce.

artworks.title: Medea Sarcophagus (Terme)
artworks.description: Another Roman Medea sarcophagus (Museo Nazionale Romano): the Corinthian catastrophe in marble — wedding gifts, fire, and the royal household Creon cannot save.

music.title: Medea
music.description: Pacini's tragedia lirica keeps Creon of Corinth in the cast of Euripides' revenge — the king whose daughter's wedding robe becomes the opera's fatal prop.

popCulture.title: Medea
popCulture.creator: Euripides
popCulture.description: Euripides makes Creon the Corinthian king who banishes Medea and dies embracing Glauce as the poisoned gifts burn — the father-in-law Jason chose over Colchis.

popCulture.title: Creon (king of Corinth)
popCulture.description: King of Corinth and father of Glauce/Creusa — not Creon son of Menoeceus, the Theban uncle of Antigone.
